verdict.rationale: Temporal can be self-hosted as a production service (Docker, Kubernetes or manual) and driven from your own application through its Client and SDKs, with Namespaces for isolation that could separate tenants. That makes it embeddable as a backend engine inside a product. But it is explicitly workflows-as-code rather than a customer-facing automation builder, and nothing in the evidence describes white-labeling, rebranding the Web UI, or exposing workflow authoring to your end customers. Missing for 10: white-label/rebranding support, an embeddable customer-facing UI or builder, documented multi-tenant embedding guidance, OEM/licensing terms, and independent corroboration of embedded deployments.
